page.title: Virtual Event Production Agency: What They Do and How to Choose
page.description: Learn what a virtual event production agency handles, typical costs, staffing models, timelines and the questions to ask before you hire.
page.h1: What does a virtual event production agency do?
page.definition: A virtual event production agency is a specialist crew that plans, rehearses, runs and wraps the operational details of webinars, summits, launches, livestreams and hybrid conferences on the platform you choose.
page.quick_answer: Hire an agency when you need a run of show, speaker rehearsals, a live producer, backup stream and edited recordings delivered on a fixed timeline without building an internal broadcast team.

sections.h2: What services are included in a typical engagement?

blocks.p: Agencies deliver the full production stack from intake through reporting, not just the streaming software.

ul: Run of show and speaker brief documents
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Full rehearsal on the live platform two to five days before the event
Live producer, Q&A moderation and platform operator during the broadcast
Backup stream ready to switch instantly
Edited recording and highlight clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours
Post-event reporting with attendance and engagement data

sections.h2: What staffing model matches my event size?

blocks.p: Crew size scales with the number of concurrent sessions, speakers and hybrid venues.

ul: Simple webinar: one producer handles run of show, platform operation and moderation
Multi-session summit: show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator
Hybrid conference: add venue AV liaison, camera operators and on-site stream engineer

sections.h2: What is the realistic timeline from kickoff to live?

blocks.p: Lead time depends on format complexity and whether the run of show is new or repeatable.

ol: Webinar: three to four weeks from brief to live
Summit or online conference: six to eight weeks from brief to live
Hybrid conference: lock venue AV and platform six to eight weeks out before finalising the agenda
One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live
Technical check 60 minutes before the broadcast starts

sections.h2: How do I evaluate and shortlist agencies?

blocks.p: Ask for evidence of the same format, platform and audience size you plan to run.

ul: Show reel or case study for a comparable webinar, summit or hybrid event
Named producer who will be on your show, not a sales contact
Clear backup stream plan and rehearsal policy
Itemised quote separating platform fees from production fees
References from clients who ran events on your chosen platform

faq.q: Do I need to buy the streaming platform before hiring an agency?
faq.a: No. The agency can help you choose and configure the platform, but the licence is a separate purchase you own. West Peek Productions does not sell event software; it produces events on the platform you select.

faq.q: Can an agency run a hybrid event with an in-person audience and a live stream?
faq.a: Yes. Hybrid productions add venue AV coordination, camera operators and an on-site stream engineer to the virtual crew. Plan six to eight weeks out to lock the venue AV and platform before the agenda is final.

faq.q: What happens if the primary stream fails during the live event?
faq.a: A production agency runs a simultaneous backup stream on a second encoder or platform. The show caller can switch sources in seconds so attendees experience minimal disruption.

faq.q: How quickly will I receive the edited recording and clips?
faq.a: Edited recordings and highlight clips are delivered within 24 to 48 hours after the event ends, while attendees still remember the content and can share it internally.

faq.q: Does the agency handle speaker coaching and slide review?
faq.a: Yes. The run of show includes a speaker brief, a branded slide template and a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live. The producer gives real-time feedback on pacing, audio and visuals.
